gen-dafont-junegull-fs-erode: Erode reads as a classic serif with a tall middle band, short ascenders and a gentle swell in its strokes. And Junegull sits above it, retro and friendly, its pinched curves making a tighter, sturdier shape than the open letters below.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-fira-sans: Junegull's lowercase stands tall as cast iron capitals, with no thick-thin flicker anywhere in sight. Fira Sans follows in a plain sans with a larger x-height, and its wide-open curves loosen up the heading's pinched ones.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-hoover: Hoover reads refined and robust, with short ascenders and a generous eye in the e. Junegull above it is retro and friendly, pinched at every curve with no hairlines or swells; a body size a notch up would let Hoover's openness show.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Tight, tall, and soft-edged. Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters close, yet its big counters and curves that refuse to close keep a paragraph warm and easy beneath Junegull's pinched retro heading.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-roundo: Roundo is a geometric sans-serif whose n matches arch to stem, with every small counter kept unclogged. And a long paragraph in it would move smoothly, a relaxed contrast to the pinched, cast-iron stance of Junegull above.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-rowan: Literary and friendly, Rowan opens every curve wide. Over a long passage its thin strokes, about half the weight of the thick ones, keep the text lively, while Junegull's taller lowercase holds the heading steady.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans brings contemporary, approachable letters with wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Spline Sans gives Junegull's retro, pinched heading a roomy partner, its sans strokes all identical in weight.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-technor: Technor glows like neon tubing, cool and geometric. Its single line thickness and wide channel into every bowl give Junegull's pinched, friendly retro heading a crisp, open counterpart, and that opposition is the pair's draw.
gen-dafont-junegull-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified and refined, its lowercase nearly as tall as its caps. But the pair's real strength is Junegull, whose strokes all carry the same visual weight, set against that low, compact serif.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-abeezee: Approachable from the first line, ABeeZee has terminals that stop well clear of the stem. Junegull is the louder one, with a retro pinched build and tall lowercase, while ABeeZee does the quiet work of keeping text open.
